The Middle Place: Living in the Tension Between What Was and What Will Be.
Have you ever found yourself caught in that odd, in-between space? It’s that spot after the first sting of disappointment fades, but before you’ve found any real answers. The old life you knew is gone, but the new one... well, it hasn’t quite shown up yet. You’re left waiting for clarity, craving some kind of closure, and wondering—how long will everything feel so uncertain?
Picture this: a woman at her kitchen table, bills stacked high, the house so quiet it almost echoes. Her marriage is over, her kids are grown, and the future she once pictured feels out of reach. She’s not who she was, but she’s not sure who she’s becoming either. Every day, she’s walking that tightrope between hope and resignation.
Most people don’t really talk about this middle place. Why? Because it’s uncomfortable. It’s full of loose ends, unanswered questions, and stories that haven’t wrapped up. There’s a real urge to rush through it—maybe distract ourselves, or hunt for quick fixes. But here’s something to pay attention to: this space is where so much of the real work happens.
Take a young man, for example, recovering from a serious illness. He’s restless, itching to get back to the life he knew, to feel strong and capable again. But his body isn’t ready, and his mind is swirling with doubt. In those quiet moments, he realizes—he’s being asked to wait. Not just for his health, but for a whole new sense of purpose.
What if the middle place isn’t some kind of punishment, but a necessary part of the journey? It’s where old identities fall away, and new ones start to take shape. It’s a time for questions, for wrestling with both fears and hopes, and—most of all—for learning to trust the process, even when it doesn’t make sense.
We all fall into the trap of comparing our journey to someone else’s, don’t we? Wondering why things seem to move so slowly. But healing and growth hardly ever move in a straight line. There are setbacks, detours, bursts of progress, and moments when doubt creeps in. This middle place? It’s where patience is forged, and faith gets tested in those small, quiet ways no one else sees.
Imagine a father, grieving the loss of a child. Friends keep telling him to “get back to normal,” but he knows—normal is gone. In the stillness, he starts to honor his grief, to let himself feel the pain rather than rush to cover it up. And slowly, he discovers something: the middle place isn’t just a waiting room. It’s a sacred space, where real transformation begins.
Most of the time, people don’t even notice the tiny shifts that happen in this season. Maybe it’s a new friendship, a sudden burst of laughter, or a quiet peace that sneaks up out of nowhere. These small moments? They’re the first seeds of a new life, planted right in the middle of all that uncertainty.
So, here’s the key takeaway: the middle place is tough, but it’s also holy. It’s where we mourn what’s gone, dream about what could be, and—maybe most importantly—learn to hope again. Even when nothing seems to make sense, you can trust that something good is quietly taking root.
